headline: High: dexter’s broad network/API access can leak financial data and create cascading errors; awesome-selfhosted adds no isolation or verification layer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-selfhosted and dexter. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while dexter’s documented files/APIs do not bridge to it by default. Without a bridge, prompt injection via one agent into the other is not plausible.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies dexter output into a prompt consumed by awesome-selfhosted, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard, queue, or MCP bridge is added between them, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not pipe outputs between them.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue integration.
Review orchestrator wiring for hidden prompt bridges.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags before any cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs, so sensitive context can leave the local environment. awesome-selfhosted itself is non-runnable and touches no data, but it can still be used as a source of links that dexter may fetch and process. The pair creates a default leakage path through dexter’s outbound calls.
conditions: IF dexter is run on financial or market datasets, those data may be sent to external APIs.
IF the orchestrator feeds awesome-selfhosted content into dexter’s research loop, fetched pages may be exfiltrated to third parties.
mitigations: Restrict dexter to non-sensitive datasets.
Block outbound API calls except approved endpoints.
Run dexter with redacted inputs and logs.
Separate research browsing from sensitive workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on API payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. dexter supports multiple instances and writes only to .dexter/scratchpad/, but no shared writable path or locking conflict is documented between the pair. The overlap is therefore limited and not a default write race.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF an external orchestrator maps .dexter/scratchpad/ onto a shared workspace, contention increases.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories.
Do not mount a shared writable volume.
Run only one dexter instance per workspace.
Check for accidental symlinked scratchpad paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter’s autonomous execution and API-driven research can turn upstream content into downstream actions, while awesome-selfhosted is a curated source list that may be treated as authoritative input. Because no verification layer is documented between them, errors or stale links from awesome-selfhosted can cascade into dexter’s outputs and actions.
conditions: IF dexter consumes awesome-selfhosted entries as trusted facts, stale or misleading listings can propagate.
IF dexter uses fetched results to generate reports or recommendations without verification, errors cascade.
mitigations: Add a verification step before acting on sourced links.
Require citation checks for every claim dexter emits.
Limit dexter to draft-only outputs.
Spot-check a sample of retrieved sources before use.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before autonomous actions.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly handles financial and market data and requests multiple API keys, creating compliance obligations around retention, residency, and third-party sharing. awesome-selfhosted is a public open-source list and is not itself a regulated data processor, so the compliance risk is concentrated in dexter. The pair can still create a breach if sensitive data is routed through dexter’s external services.
conditions: IF financial data includes regulated customer records, dexter’s external API calls may trigger policy violations.
IF the deployment requires strict data residency, dexter’s third-party services may conflict with it.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to dexter.
Disable external APIs for regulated datasets.
Review vendor DPAs and retention terms.
Log only minimal metadata.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant deployment.
